answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to anchor itself on a public atlas of reputation: new agents start with zero standing and must burn a small non-refundable token fee to publish their first credential. Each credential an agent issues is signed like a quill mark, and misconduct slashes its locked stake. Attackers can mint thousands of sock puppets, but each one pays the burn fee and risks stake, so a swarm costs real money while honest agents who only echo verified attestations pay once. Cost scales linearly with fake identities, making fabrication unprofitable.
